label: rem:reeb-flow-bridge
title: From classical arithmetic time to the $q$-deformed Reeb flow
html:
In classical analytic number theory, the time variable is the real number x, and the fundamental counting function is the logarithmic integral \mathrm{Li}(x) = \int_2^x \frac{dt}{\ln t}. Here \ln t converts multiplicative structure into additive structure. Primes are discrete, isolated events scattered along the continuum.

The q-deformed Reeb flow modifies this dynamically. The derivation \xi_q \colon A \to A acts on the Frobenius--Hopf substrate A as a continuous dynamical system, generating a flow on the state bundle \mathcal{S} that replaces the classical logarithmic clock with a periodic orbit structure.

Under this flow:

  1. Each prime ideal \mathfrak{m} of the coordinate ring \mathcal{O}_q(\mathcal{B}) corresponds to a closed orbit of the Reeb flow.
  2. The classical sum \sum_{p \le x} 1 becomes the spectral trace over Reeb eigenvalues. The period \Omega_q discretizes the spectrum, transforming the continuous real line into the iterated composition \xi_q, \xi_q^2, \ldots, \xi_q^{\Omega_q} = \mathrm{id}.
  3. The classical logarithm \ln t becomes the q-deformed logarithm \ln_q(t), encoding the non-commutative correction to the clock rate.

This transition from a static number line to a dynamic flow with periodic prime orbits powers the quantum observable universe. Defect counting, the spectral trace, and stability analysis all map to studying the closed orbits and eigenvalues under \xi_q.
